QF.id: AIFM Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_4

question.text: Mr. Ajay Menon and Ms. Kavita Rao are two LPs in Godavari Category II AIF. Mr. Menon demands a higher expected return before accepting a more volatile asset. Ms. Rao evaluates investments solely on expected return and treats variance as irrelevant to her decision (i.e., she requires zero risk premium for accepting additional variance). How would Modern Portfolio Theory classify them respectively?

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 4.3 of the workbook (p. 55) defines a risk-averse investor as one who demands a greater risk premium for greater risk - Menon's behaviour. A risk-neutral investor requires zero risk premium for additional variance and evaluates investments solely on expected return - the operational definition built into Rao's profile in the (updated) stem. The section title at p. 63 also identifies "risk-neutral investors" as a distinct category. The Trap: Confusing risk-neutral with risk-averse is the classic exam trap. A risk-seeking investor would actually pay a premium for variance - this is not what either LP exhibits. Note: The original stem's wording of Rao as "indifferent to variance" was loose because the workbook does not provide a direct definition of risk-neutral on the checked pages (54-56, 63). The stem has been tightened to define risk-neutral operationally (zero risk premium required for additional variance), so the classification follows directly from the workbook's definition of risk-averse and the residual risk-neutral category named at p. 63. Source: FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 55, 63.
